title: SemiSAM+: Rethinking Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation in the Era of Foundation Models
mechanism: A trainable specialist generates prompts for frozen SAM-type generalists, and their masks supervise the specialist on unlabelled images.
adaptation: Inactive only (blobby, well labelled, 42 train cells). The house model proposes inactive boxes on pool cells; SAM2/SAM3 refines them; keep masks that agree with the house mask at IoU > 0.7 as extra inactive training cells. Not for thin cracks.
min_experiment: Arm house PF + SAM-refined inactive pool cells vs house PF, 5 seeds. Metric: inactive IoU on clean-49, module-grouped 5-fold CV, and E1. Kill if inactive IoU gains less than 0.03 in CV.
evidence: R: two public sets plus one in-house set; gains reported mainly with extremely scarce labels. Numbers not on the abstract page.
prior_overlap: SAM as a pseudo-label refiner was never run. Our Mean Teacher at 5% labels helped inactive (+0.11). Open.

alt_notes.adaptation: House PF predictions on pool half-cells prompt SAM2/SAM3; keep FM masks where location agrees but FM gives region extent (inactive); expected low value at 478 labels.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + SemiSAM+-style FM-refined pseudo-labels on pool half-cells vs PF + raw house pseudo-labels; H36 inactive IoU; kill under margin M.
